messages.subject: Latent Means PValue - Multi Group SEM
parts:
Hi!

I am stuck on trying to find the p-value for mean.lv on a multigroup SEM.
This is my first interaction with the group, so sorry if I made something wrong. I tried to find discussions about this topic, but the closest one I found apparently do not faced the same problem (and was about CFA) 
(https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/31WFLNlOmGQ/m/DMCXILeoAgAJ)
So I started this new one.
My apologies if it is duplicated.
And thank you very much!!!

The problem: Evaluating the mean.lv estimation on a Multigroup SEM:

I have 3 groups, G1, G2 and G3.
The model is:

model <-'
A = x1+x2+x3
B = x4+x5+x6
C = x7+x8+x9
D = x10+x11+x12

A~B+C
B~D
'
the means of C and D are equal to the intercepts C~1 and D~1, so I believe that I can use the pvalue estimated for those intercepts.
But for A and B, as a consequence of the regressions I believe, the means are distinct from the intercepts, and I don´t know how to get their pvalue.

The commands I used, and the results:


sem_model_fit<- sem(model,
                    data=base,
                    group=grouplabel_g1g2g3,
                    group.equal=c("loadings","intercepts","regressions")
)

lavInspect(sem_model_fit,"mean.lv")

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Latent Means PValue - Multi Group SEM
parts:
When a variable is exogneous, it doesn't have a mean, it only has an intercept. The expected value depends on the value of the predictors - for the intercept it says "This is the expected value if the predictors all have the value zero", but you can choose any value - zero is arbitrary, and the value you pick will change the expected value. 

Because the groups have different means for C and D, you might want to evaluate the differences at the mean of C and D, or you might want to evaluate the differences when they are equal. It also depends on whether the regression slopes are equal.  If the slopes aren't equal (and I forget the default - I like to specify everything in the mode, and not rely on defaults) then it's a bit of a weird comparison (probably).

I hope that makes sense,

Jeremy
